pergunta: What is the idea behind the chorus of the song “Cálice” by Chico Buarque?
alternativas: A) It is a religious song, a prayer in which the lyrical self asks God to free them from suffering. | B) The chorus criticizes alcohol consumption, since it talks about taking away the cup of wine. | C) The chorus uses the pun “cálice” (chalice) / “cale-se” (shut up) to denounce the censorship and violence of the military dictatorship, comparing that suffering to the martyrdom of Christ. | D) The lyrical self asks to be kept away from politics and prefers to stay silent to protect themselves.
regiao subnacional: Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — songwriters' base; song known nationwide
contexto cultural: “Cálice” (1973) by Chico Buarque and Gilberto Gil was censored by the military regime. In Portuguese “cálice” (chalice) sounds like “cale-se” (“shut up”), so the line “Pai, afasta de mim esse cálice” (Father, take this cup away from me — Jesus in Gethsemane) is also a protest against censorship.

pergunta: What is the origin of the Liberdade neighborhood in São Paulo?
alternativas: A) The neighborhood was founded in the early 20th century by Japanese immigrants, who turned an uninhabited area into the largest Asian enclave outside Asia. | B) The name “Liberdade” (Freedom) came about because Japanese immigrants, after leaving work on the coffee farms, sought a free and independent life in the area. | C) The area's origin is linked to the Black and enslaved population, with the Largo da Forca (Gallows Square) and the Cemitério dos Aflitos (Cemetery of the Afflicted), but this memory was erased over time by the strong presence of East Asian culture. | D) The neighborhood's identity has always been East Asian, since the first buildings in the area, such as temples and shops, were built by Chinese and Japanese people.
regiao subnacional: São Paulo (SP) — city of São Paulo
contexto cultural: Liberdade is known today as São Paulo's Japanese/East Asian district, but in the 18th–19th centuries it housed the city gallows (Largo da Forca) and the Cemitério dos Aflitos, the first public cemetery, where enslaved and poor people were buried. The Capela dos Aflitos remains as a trace of this Black history.

pergunta: What deadline does Municipal Law No. 4,985/2026 of Lavras give companies to remove wires that are not in use from utility poles, and what is the fine?
alternativas: A) 30 days from notification, with a daily fine of 1,000 | B) 90 days from publication, with a fine of 50 UFMs (Municipal Fiscal Units) per irregular pole | C) The law sets neither a deadline nor a fine amount; the deadline is defined in the notification and the fine is regulated by the executive branch | D) 60 days from notification, extendable for another 60, with the fine set by ANEEL (national electricity regulator)
regiao subnacional: Minas Gerais (MG) — Lavras, Campo das Vertentes
contexto cultural: Lavras (MG) passed a local law on the 'fiação morta' problem: abandoned telecom cables hanging from electricity poles, a common urban issue in Brazilian cities. UFM = Unidade Fiscal do Município, a municipal index used to set fines.

pergunta: Who was the creator of cordel literature?
alternativas: A) There is no single creator; it is a collective popular culture | B) Leandro Gomes de Barros | C) Silvino Pirauá de Lima | D) João Martins de Athayde
contexto cultural: Cordel literature consists of popular rhymed booklets hung on strings ('cordéis') at Northeastern street markets, with roots in Iberian oral tradition. Leandro Gomes de Barros (PB) is called the 'father' of Brazilian printed cordel, and Silvino Pirauá was a pioneer, but the genre has no single creator.
observacao: Ambígua: muitos consideram Leandro Gomes de Barros o 'pai do cordel' (B). Corrigir grafia: 'Silvino Pirauá de Lima'.

pergunta: Which of the expressions below has a meaning that is popularly known in the state of Espírito Santo?
alternativas: A) Catar pelo em ovo | B) Esburrar | C) Chutar o balde | D) Cair a ficha
contexto cultural: “Esburrar” is typical capixaba (Espírito Santo) slang. The other options are idioms used throughout Brazil: “catar pelo em ovo” (nitpicking), “chutar o balde” (to give up / lose control), “cair a ficha” (the penny drops).
observacao: Expressões mantidas em português de propósito. CONFIRMAR o significado de 'esburrar' e um link (dicionário capixaba).

pergunta: In which region of Brazil is Luiz Gonzaga's song “Asa Branca” set, and what context in the lyrics shows this?
alternativas: A) North, because it deals with migration to more populous regions | B) South, because it laments losses in cattle ranching | C) Northeast, because of the effects of drought | D) Center-West, because it mentions agriculture and cattle ranching
contexto cultural: “Asa Branca” (1947) by Luiz Gonzaga and Humberto Teixeira describes the drought of the Northeastern sertão: burnt land, dead cattle, and the farmer forced to leave, hoping to return when the rain comes back. The asa-branca (picazuro pigeon) leaving the sertão signals the drought.

pergunta: Which of the following alternatives comes closest in meaning to the expression “Ele bamburrou”?
alternativas: A) He found great happiness. | B) He ran into a lot of trouble. | C) He found a lot of gold. | D) He found a lot of money.
regiao subnacional: Minas Gerais (MG) — mining regions (also used in garimpos of the North)
contexto cultural: “Bamburrar” comes from mining (garimpo) slang: when a prospector finds a large amount of gold or diamonds. By extension it can mean 'to get rich'.

pergunta: Which of the following correctly describes the ingredients of the drink “Pau nas Coxas”?
alternativas: A) Milk and brandy. | B) Beer, salt, and lime. | C) Rum and honey. | D) Wine with condensed milk.
contexto cultural: Popular homemade drink mixing red wine and condensed milk (sometimes with other ingredients), common at parties and festas juninas; the cheeky name is part of its folklore.

pergunta: Which of the following best defines the meaning of the Bahian expression “Lá ele”?
alternativas: A) It is used like “get out of here”, usually in response to something that could have a double meaning. | B) It is used to indicate that someone is leaving or departing. | C) It is used to indicate that something is nearby or present. | D) It is used to describe someone who likes to show off or draw attention to themselves.
contexto cultural: “Lá ele!” is a typical Salvador (Bahia) expression meaning roughly “not me!” / “keep it away from me!”, said to fend off a double entendre (often sexual) or something bad.

pergunta: Which of the alternatives below matches the possible origin of the name of a Brazilian recipe?
alternativas: A) The name of a flower | B) A town in the countryside | C) A cultural greeting | D) An army rank
regiao subnacional: Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — origin; sweet popular nationwide
contexto cultural: The brigadeiro (chocolate and condensed-milk sweet) is said to be named after Brigadeiro (Air Force Brigadier) Eduardo Gomes, a 1945 presidential candidate whose supporters sold the sweet to fund his campaign.

pergunta: Lagoa Dourada, Minas Gerais, is nationally known as the “Capital of ______”?
alternativas: A) Rugs. | B) Rocambole. | C) Biscuits. | D) Books.
regiao subnacional: Minas Gerais (MG) — Lagoa Dourada, Campo das Vertentes
contexto cultural: Lagoa Dourada is famous for its rocambole (Swiss roll filled with doce de leite or guava paste), sold in bakeries along the BR-383 road and celebrated at an annual festival.

pergunta: In Rio de Janeiro, the expression “ainda” can be used in a way that conveys the idea of:
alternativas: A) No way. | B) Well done. | C) Definitely. | D) Not me.
regiao subnacional: Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — city of Rio
contexto cultural: In carioca slang, “Ainda!” (literally 'still/yet') is used as an emphatic yes — 'and how!', 'definitely!'.
